content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the branch centerline with a series of seat points along its curve, defining their coordinates to shape the overall form.

I'm checking that the koala's rump sits naturally into the branch curvature, sinking slightly at the hip point without clipping below the surface.

Now I'm working out a helper function to get the branch's y-position at any given z-coordinate, and defining a grip arc function so the koala's hands and feet can wrap convincingly around the branch's circumference based on its local tangent direction.

I'm figuring out rotation directions for the left and right hands wrapping over the branch top, treating the branch's forward direction as roughly the Z-axis so I can use consistent rotation signs for each hand's finger curl, then building the finger joint chains along those arcs and sizing the grip radius against the branch's actual radius at that point.

Now I'm working out the hand's palm geometry—placing a thick capsule from the wrist joint to the finger roots at the correct offset from the branch surface, then staggering three finger chains along the z-axis so they wrap naturally around the grip.

Still figuring out the finger joint naming and count conventions...

I'm estimating the total joint budget: 5 chains of 3 joints per hand across 4 limbs plus body gives roughly 90 joints, comfortably under the 160 limit, and now I'm thinking through how koala feet should have an opposable big toe plus fused digits.

For the hind feet I'll try 4 over-top toes with two visually merged, plus 1 opposable big toe underneath, each getting 3 joints, which pushes the digit total to around 60 plus limbs and spine—still under budget. To trim further, I could simplify each toe chain to just 2 points (1 span, joint + tip) instead of 3, cutting bend complexity while keeping the look.

For claws I'm adding a spike at each toe tip using the chain's end tangent as direction, sized small with a thin radius. For the fur, I'm using a cellPaint function seeded per body region, with paws rendered in a darker charcoal tone contrasted against lighter fur, and the fingers/paw pads kept mostly bare and dark like a real koala's.

Now I'm working out head geometry: placing the neck base and head joint close together given a short neck, then sizing a skull box around the head joint so it spans roughly y 1.08–1.25 and z 0.025–0.195, with ears reaching up to about 1.30. I'm checking that the total sit height comes out around 0.7, which feels a bit large but fits a stylized big-headed look, then positioning a muzzle box projecting forward from the face.

Continuing to refine the muzzle, nose, and lower jaw boxes, adjusting their centers and dimensions so the nose sits above and in front of the muzzle, the jaw tucks below as a chin, and everything stays roughly aligned without excessive overlap with the skull -- also planning a small white fur tuft card for the chin. I'm about to position the eyes symmetrically on the front of the skull.

Setting the earL joint with an outward hinge, then adding eyebrow/forehead tufts and cheek fluff cards using a spiky white-grey pixel texture, scattered across the lower sides of the head box by filtering surface normals.

I'm also adding fur cards to the body: scattering grey tuft textures across the torso with cream accents at the chest and rump, and tinting the grey texture per card to match fur color using a paint-read-once approach.

Designing tuft pixel pattern...

Building the skeleton rig with joints and chains...

Working out the skull center position and jaw joint placement using local offsets from the head, checking the spans stay within the target bounding ranges.

Now I'm setting up the arm chains for each side, computing shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions with the limb helper, using an outward-and-back bend direction hint for the elbow and building the joint chain with proper parent and naming.

I'm then tapering radii from shoulder down to wrist for the fur paint, and moving on to the hind legs, working out hip, knee, and ankle target positions for each side similarly.

For the hind leg IK, I'm computing bend hints and checking distances to make sure the knee bends outward correctly given the short reach relative to limb lengths. Then I'm naming the leg joint chain (hip, knee, ankle) with the foot digits parenting off the ankle tip.

For foot placement, I'm checking that feet at z=0.05 might intersect the belly volume near the hip sphere, so I'm nudging zF to 0.08 to stay clear, and setting hand heights separately. I'm also confirming the thighs splay outward from hip to knee to match a koala's astride sitting posture, then moving on to the toes.

Now I'm working out the toe geometry: each foot's digits are arcs around the branch axis, mirroring the hand setup but with slightly larger radius since feet are bigger, with four toes over the top and one underneath, staggered along the branch width. I'm defining the foot pad as a connecting rod from ankle to toe roots, then setting up the arc centers along the branch axis for each toe.

I realize I should use the actual tangent vector at each point along the branch rather than assuming a fixed axis, since the branch has slope -- computing the perpendicular offset relative to the true tangent keeps the toe arcs correctly oriented as they wrap over the branch.

I'm working out thumb arcs and radii relative to the branch, then figuring out palm placement — positioning the wrist behind and outward from the finger root with a capsule connecting them, and setting the arm target to the wrist position.

I'm planning to skip detailed paw pad texturing for now and move toward writing actual code rather than overanalyzing proportions. Next I'm sketching out a twig-building function that sweeps a Catmull-Rom path through given points with a tapered radius for the branch material.

I realize I need to be careful with leaf frames—since literal position/normal inputs default to the nearest joint's bone, leaves near the koala's head could accidentally inherit head-bone rigging instead of staying fixed to the stand. So I'll explicitly pass a `bone: stand` option everywhere for stand-related geometry (twigs, leaf cards, sweeps) to force them rigid on the correct bone, and vary leaf orientation along the path with an alternating flow direction rather than true randomness.

For gumnuts I'm placing small tan spheres with caps at twig points, bound to the stand bone. For bark peels, I'm generating hanging strip cards around the trunk's surface using outward-facing frames from the trunk sweep, with some lean variation and a downward flow, textured with a tan strip pattern and darker edges.

I'm adding color variation with browns and creams for two bark texture variants, plus moss and lichen patches painted near the trunk base. For the head, I'm setting up a skin layout for skull, nose, muzzle, and jaw boxes on a single UV sheet, then writing a fur-fill helper that assigns grey-based colors with random spread and dithering across each face rectangle.

I need to make sure the sheet colors align with the limited flat-color palette budget, since textures and paints don't count against that limit but named flat colors do. Now I'm planning the skull face details -- a fur gradient darker on top and lighter on the cheeks, a brow band, and a small black eye with a darker surrounding ring.

For the eye highlight, I'm adding a single white pixel near the top-right corner of the black eye to give it a tiny sparkle. For the cheeks, I'm computing a dithered whiteness value based on distance from the edge using blended horizontal and vertical factors, then picking a shade from the grey palette accordingly.

I'm now setting up the remaining faces: the side ear patches get lighter near the cheek, the top of the head stays darker grey fur with a subtly lighter center, the back face gets plain fur shading, and the underside stays pale. For the muzzle, I'm giving the front face a pale cream tone with a dark mouth line near the bottom and a couple of dark whisker dots, while the nose box gets a black gradient with its own highlight, and the jaw box front face is shaping up as creamy white for the chin.

Now I'm detailing the ear construction: painting the outer disc with fur grey and the inner disc with a cream-white speckled pattern plus a darker rim, then adding a ring of outward-facing fluff cards along the inner rim to create a fringe effect.

With that settled, I'm moving on to the stand dressing — stacking tiled slabs for a base (dark walnut) and a lighter top layer, positioning them so each sits flush on the one below.

Now I'm filling in the rest: brass corner brackets and screws merged as one part, a plaque plane on the front, a lathe-turned root flange with a bolt ring, and then scattering fallen leaves, pebbles, and moss clumps for ground litter.

For the trunk I'm defining the sweep path with a tapering radius array from base to top, bending slightly for a natural lean, and noting where the seat branch splits off around y=0.40.

Now I'm plotting the upper limbs: one curving right from the trunk near y=0.92 tapering outward, another on the opposite side branching near y=1.12, checking they clear the koala's ear placement without overlap, then tallying total tree height from these branch points.

With leafy twig clusters fanning at each limb's end and near the seat branch tip to frame the koala's face, I'm now moving into writing a helper function for generating twig geometry with hanging leaves.

Writing twig sweep function...

Adjusting leaf texture dimensions to match pixel density, then working out row ordering so the texture's top-to-bottom layout maps correctly to the leaf's stem-to-tip direction.

Writing leaf shape math...

For bark, I'm texturing the strip cards with a tan 4x9 pattern, and for body fur I'm scattering tuft cards over the body sweep surface, filtering hits by normal direction to keep them on the upper/outer faces with default fur coloring.

No whiskers needed for koalas, but I'm adding cheek tufts by scattering hits over the skull surface filtered by normal angle and low y position, plus setting claw and paw color constants.

Writing fur gradient colors...

Now I'm defining the belly/chest cream patch logic, restricting it by y-range and front-facing normal while narrowing the x bounds so limbs don't accidentally pick up the same coloring.

Now I'm working on the paws with a dark dithered ramp, then moving to the bark texture with noisy color streaks, and finally sketching out a wood-plank plinth tile using sine-based row variation for the plank coloring.

Writing wood plank texture...

For the plaque, I'll use a plane geometry with pixel art text texture facing outward. I'm mostly skipping explicit naming for pieces, and giving plinth parts bone attachments with explicit positions so the geometry origin aligns correctly. Now I'm writing the actual file, typing out chain paths and sweep radius functions for the limb geometry.

Writing finger and digit code...

Sampling arc points at three parameter values to round the polyline corners works fine, and Vector3 arrays should satisfy the Points type. For claws I'll orient them along the tangent at the digit's end so they curl downward, and I'll stagger hand/foot z-positions slightly between left and right before diving into writing the actual code.

Writing branch radius function...

For the spine sweep I'm using the chain as the source path, running from hips to neckbase, and defining rx/ry radius functions over that parameter range.

I'm sweeping the thigh and leg with tapering radii keyed at hip, knee, and ankle, making sure the hip joint sits inside the body radius for a smooth blend. For hind feet I'm placing an ankle tip and a short pad capsule leading to the digits, plus a heel lump. Then I'm setting up leaf card textures lying flat with mirroring before writing everything to the file.
